note: Tys's standing rules as data (docs/TASTE.md says what each one does, why, and the day it came from). Every rule has an id, a kind, its data and a one-line reason. The app reads this file at every Make and re-cut (a change needs no restart); a missing or broken file means no rules at all. To drop a rule, delete it or give it "off": true. Kinds: subject (stills whose noun holds one of the words, as whole words, are never picked by the app; except spares a phrase; head: true reads only the noun's head, so a skull with horns is a skull), family (whole catalogue families never picked), run (at most max stills of the group in one cut), look (a look kept but demoted: a note, the back of the pool, or an effect that steps aside), limit (a cap on a knob or a picker), weight (the order families are drawn in).

rules.reason: A cup or a jug is a plain household thing to morph; the first montage opened on two and they fell flat.
Wheels of every kind went on the veto list after the first montage; a wheel of fortune was swapped for the scales.
The acoustic guitar was the plainest object in the first montage's run of instruments.
A run of instruments in a row (pianos into guitars) had no reason to be in the song; one instrument a cut at most.
The None vibe took the myths literally and gave a wig (the golden fleece renders as one), a helmet and hay: dull objects.
The lava dinosaur stretch was the one part of the montage he disliked, and not for the first time.
The pirate run had no link to the song: a hat, a ship in a bottle and a pistol in a row.
The parrot rendered wrong.
The binoculars came with no context and held the screen too long; the spyglass is what renders as them.
The crab rendered like a cartoon, and came twice in one stretch.
A famous building dropped into a chain (the Taj Mahal) is dull and out of place; the moai and Stonehenge stayed.
The neon Egypt look with the sphinx and the snake is out; the scarab stays, it is a favourite.
A horn turned up at random among the chrome relics (the ram's golden horns) and read as plain.
A plain lightning bolt turned up at random among the chrome relics.
The DNA turning into a black glass heart was unpleasant to watch, and the black heart itself unattractive.
The hat and the clock in the gold stretch were generic, with nothing symbolic about them.
The cups-and-jugs family (teapots, kettles, shakers, glasses): plain household vessels, generic in any vibe.
Wet paint is one of the weakest vibes and its colour scheme does not work; it stays, off the featured cards, for anyone who picks it.
The pink odd-machine and its theme are out of his cuts; it stays in the registry, behind More vibes.
Chess pieces in plain marble were dull; they go to the back of a marble cut instead of opening it.
Black-and-white film clips do not react to the music and read flat in a music video; the montage dropped them.
The kaleidoscope was overused, and on the fish it flattened them into a pattern: a shot that morphs a living thing plays without it.
Above Chaos 0.5 the kick wobble and the orbit swing read as shaky hand-held camera work; the montage capped it there.
The opening is the hook and it should be calm and consistent: the natural opener ran at Intensity 0.6 or under.
White flashes are intense enough to be rare accents: no flash look before the first drop, the first one arrives with it.
The sliced foreshadow draws bars, part of the repeated bar transition he grew tired of; the trace does the same job.
No transition type twice in a row: the same handoff again and again is what made the bars repetitive.
The strip wipe was overused; the montage kept wipes under a quarter of its handoffs.
The strobe cut is the loudest handoff there is: only on the main drop, never on a lesser one.
Effects are optional and sparing; the montage never stacked two on one look, so a cut's effects take turns.
No image repeats in a cut: two stills of the same object (a second seahorse) count as a repeat too.
Nothing shown twice in a montage: a song plan or a batch of variations never uses one vibe twice.
A Make is clips or objects, never both: a film clip dissolving into a still read as two videos stitched together.
One palette per cut: a pink rose blooming among black glass flowers made the opener uneven.
Natural subjects worked best in the montage, and an object should carry a symbol: living and iconic families come first.
